about.probMissingAccountabilityDesc: When ownership is unclear, delays and disputes compound without a traceable record.
about.probDelayedReportingDesc: Field progress reaches the office late — decisions lag behind what already happened on site.
about.probPoorVisibilityDesc: Managers and stakeholders lack a current picture of progress, risks, and open items.
about.probDocumentChaosDesc: Reports, photos, and approvals live in different tools with weak links between them.
about.probReactiveDecisionsDesc: Teams firefight instead of acting on structured evidence and agreed workflows.
about.whySubtitle: Our product philosophy — not a feature list. See the platform page for capability detail.
about.whyOneRecordDesc: Projects, reports, evidence, and approvals connect in one workspace — not another silo.
about.whyFieldToOfficeDesc: What happens on site reaches managers and configured stakeholders without manual reconstruction.
about.whyStructuredReportingDesc: Daily reports and tasks follow consistent formats teams can review and compare over time.
about.whyEvidenceFirstDesc: Photos and documentation support claims — reducing disputes and rework.
about.whyAiAssistedReviewDesc: Analysis highlights gaps and risks for human review — not autonomous project changes.
about.whyDecisionSupportDesc: Managers get clearer context to approve, escalate, or request changes — accountability stays human.

about.principleEvidenceDesc: Claims should be backed by reports, photos, and approvals — not hallway assumptions.
about.principleHumanAccountabilityDesc: People approve actions; the product supports review — it does not replace responsibility.
about.principleVisibilityDesc: Teams deserve a current operational picture — not reconstructed status from memory.

faq.coreSubtitle: Basics teams ask before committing to a pilot.
faq.coreWhatIsA: A construction operations platform for projects, field reports, photo evidence, approvals, and manager review — with AI assistance where enabled. It is not a generic chat tool or a spreadsheet replacement alone.
faq.coreWhoForA: General contractors, project managers, and field teams who need one operational record from site to office. Stakeholder/owner views are available when you configure them — they are not the same as internal contractor finance views.
faq.coreWorkerTrainingA: Field apps follow structured daily-report flows. Most teams onboard with a short walkthrough on start work, photos, and submit — not a multi-week training program.
faq.coreIosAndroidQ: Can we use Android and iPhone?
faq.coreIosAndroidA: AiStroyka Manager and Worker are the primary iOS apps for pilot and production use. Android mirrors exist in the roadmap; confirm device support with us before you standardize on Android in the field.
faq.coreReportingA: Workers and managers capture daily reports and photo evidence on site. Data syncs to the platform for review and approval. See the mobile page for the field workflow — this FAQ stays at the adoption level.
faq.coreAiManagersA: AI can summarize reports, highlight risks, and flag missing evidence for review. It supports decisions — it does not replace manager approval. See the copilot page for assistant workflows, not photo-analysis depth.
faq.opsSubtitle: Rollout and day-to-day use on active construction.
faq.opsImplementationA: Most pilots start with one project, roles, and reporting templates. Timing depends on your team size and data migration — we scope this in a pilot plan rather than promising a fixed go-live date.
faq.opsActiveProjectsQ: Can it work on active projects?
faq.opsActiveProjectsA: Yes. Teams often start on live sites with a defined scope: daily reporting, approvals, and manager review first — then expand modules as the pilot proves fit.
faq.opsApprovalsA: Reports and documents move through review and approval steps with a traceable record. Managers approve, request changes, or escalate — actions stay accountable.
faq.opsInternetQ: What happens if internet is unstable?
faq.opsInternetA: Field capture is designed for site conditions; sync runs when connectivity returns. Do not assume full offline parity for every workflow until we confirm it for your pilot scope.
faq.opsManagerReviewA: Managers use web or mobile manager surfaces: an inbox of pending submissions, photos in context, and approve or request-changes flows.
faq.opsOwnerProgressA: Configured stakeholder or owner views can show progress and customer-facing commercial artifacts you choose to expose — not internal contractor costs, margin, or internal budget pressure.
faq.trustSubtitle: Access, AI guardrails, and human accountability.
faq.trustDataVisibilityA: Data is scoped to your tenant and project membership. Users see what their role allows — field teams, managers, admins, and configured external viewers are not interchangeable.
faq.trustAccessControlA: Role-based access with tenant isolation. Permissions govern who can capture, review, approve, and configure stakeholder visibility.
faq.trustAiAutonomousA: No. AI outputs are recommendations and summaries for review. The product does not silently change approvals, tasks, or project records without human action.
faq.trustHumanReviewA: Yes. Approvals, rejections, and material changes stay with people who are accountable. AI assists analysis; managers and authorized roles decide.

security.accessApiTenantDesc: Authenticated `/api/v1/*` routes derive tenant context from membership; service-role JWTs are rejected on user paths.
security.accessStakeholderPortalDesc: Portal-only users are redirected away from internal workspace, billing, admin, and contractor finance routes.
security.accessAuthProvidersDesc: Email/password and configured OAuth providers (e.g. Apple, Telegram when enabled). Leaked-password checks can be enabled on Supabase Auth.
security.accessSsoDesc: SAML/OIDC single sign-on — planned for enterprise rollout; not a self-serve toggle today.
security.aiGovernanceSubtitle: How construction AI handles your content — human review, consent, and guardrails.
security.aiHumanReviewDesc: AI outputs are recommendations and summaries for managers to review — not autonomous project changes.
security.aiNoSilentChangesDesc: Copilot and analysis do not silently approve tasks, change orders, or project records without human action.
security.aiTrainingOptInDesc: Model-improvement use of tenant data requires explicit opt-in on the tenant record. Default is deny; export gates enforce consent.

workflows.pathOverdueFollowupDesc: Overdue tasks surface in dashboards and manager actions. Escalation chains are manual today — no automatic outbound escalation.
workflows.pathMissingEvidenceDesc: Missing photo evidence appears in insights and manager action lists. Requesting updates stays a human review step.
workflows.pathReportAnalysisDesc: Submitting a report notifies managers and queues analysis jobs. Report-level analysis is partial — see Construction AI for depth.
workflows.pathRiskAlertDesc: Risk signals appear in operational views. Tenant-configurable threshold alerts and rules-engine actions are planned.
workflows.timelineSubtitle: How operational signals move through the product today — automation expands only where labeled LIVE or PARTIAL.
workflows.stepSignalDesc: Issues, overdue tasks, missing evidence, and submitted reports enter structured records — not chat-only updates.
workflows.stepRouteDesc: Manager notifications and stakeholder delivery fire for supported events. Coverage is partial — not every signal routes automatically.
workflows.stepReviewDesc: Managers approve or reject reports and documents, request changes, and close issues — accountable human decisions.
workflows.stepAutomateDesc: Trigger-to-action rules, outbound escalation, and tenant risk alerting are scaffold-only today — planned, not live BPM.
workflows.stepAuditDesc: Approval events, document decisions, and traceability records leave a review-ready history in the tenant workspace.
workflows.liveSubtitle: Governed operational paths you can rely on in production — human review included by design.
workflows.liveManualReviewDesc: Submitted reports and documents awaiting decision appear in unified manager approval queues.
workflows.liveManagerNotificationsDesc: In-app inbox for report submissions, issue updates, assignments, and selected operational events.
workflows.liveIssueRecordsDesc: Project issues with status history and manager notification on create and status change.
workflows.liveReportQueuesDesc: Field report submission with manager notify-on-submit and approval workflow events.
workflows.liveProjectRecordsDesc: Tasks, milestones, timeline events, and structured project status — the source for workflow signals.
workflows.roadmapSubtitle: Capabilities on the roadmap or limited today — never marketed as full automation.
workflows.roadmapWorkflowTriggersDesc: Webhook and domain events can publish signals; end-to-end trigger-to-action rules are not fully wired.
workflows.roadmapAutoRemindersDesc: Stakeholder invite and client-request reminders run on scheduled jobs — finite kinds, not a generic reminder platform.
workflows.roadmapRiskAlertingDesc: Operational risk views exist; tenant threshold alerts via rules engine are planned.
workflows.roadmapOutboundEscalationDesc: Overdue and risk follow-up stays manager-driven today — automatic escalation chains are planned.
workflows.roadmapAutomationEngineDesc: Configurable rules engine and action dispatcher are scaffold-only — planned replacement for noop handlers.

enterprise.title: Enterprise
enterprise.metaDescription: Enterprise readiness for large construction organizations — governance, security, AI oversight, rollout, and evaluation. Not a product catalog or pricing page.
enterprise.heroTitle: Can AISTROYKA be adopted by a large organization?
enterprise.heroSubtitle: Evaluate governance, security, AI oversight, and rollout readiness — how large teams assess fit before expansion. For product modules see Features; for commercial engagement see Pricing.
enterprise.governanceSubtitle: How roles, access, audit trails, and visibility work at organizational scale — not a feature list.
enterprise.govRoleGovernanceDesc: Managers, field teams, admins, and configured viewers operate under distinct roles — permissions govern capture, review, approval, and stakeholder visibility.
enterprise.govAccessControlDesc: Tenant-scoped membership and project access — who can see, edit, approve, or configure external views is governed, not ad hoc.
enterprise.govAuditabilityDesc: Reports, approvals, and evidence leave a traceable record for review — readiness for organizations that require accountability, not chat-only updates.
enterprise.govProjectVisibilityDesc: Office and field align on operational truth — stakeholder views can be configured without exposing internal contractor finance.
enterprise.securitySubtitle: Enterprise data boundaries — how isolation, handling, and permissions support adoption. See Security and FAQ for depth.
enterprise.secTenantIsolationDesc: Workspaces are scoped to your organization — data and AI context stay within tenant and project membership boundaries.
enterprise.secDataHandlingDesc: Encryption in transit and at rest with auditable access. Model training on tenant content requires explicit opt-in — default deny. See Security for depth.
enterprise.secPermissionsDesc: Role-based permissions govern every surface — field capture, manager review, admin configuration, and external viewer access.
enterprise.secOperationalTransparencyDesc: Leaders see current operational status from structured records — not reconstructed status from scattered channels.
enterprise.aiSubtitle: How Construction AI and Copilot behave under enterprise oversight — human review and controlled recommendations, not autonomous decisions.
enterprise.aiHumanReviewDesc: AI outputs are recommendations for authorized reviewers — approvals and material changes stay with accountable people.
enterprise.aiExplainableFindingsDesc: Analysis surfaces deviations, risks, and evidence gaps tied to project context — review-ready, not opaque scores.
enterprise.aiReviewWorkflowsDesc: Manager review paths for reports, photos, and AI findings — governed steps before outcomes enter the audit trail.
enterprise.aiControlledRecommendationsDesc: Copilot assists managers within tenant boundaries — summaries and guidance scoped to your workspace, not generic chat.
enterprise.rolloutSubtitle: Organizational adoption across projects and sites — readiness topics, not implementation phase detail.
enterprise.rollMultiProjectDesc: Shared governance, roles, and reporting consistency across active sites — evaluate fit before broad deployment.
enterprise.rollStakeholderVisibilityDesc: Configure owner and stakeholder views on progress and commercial artifacts you choose to expose — without internal cost exposure.
enterprise.rollOrganizationalAdoptionDesc: Field and office roles onboard with structured capture and review — adoption checkpoints for multi-team rollout.
enterprise.rollChangeManagementDesc: Expand modules, sites, or integrations when readiness criteria are met — phased change, not big-bang cutover.
enterprise.evaluationSubtitle: How large organizations assess readiness — distinct from Pricing commercial terms and discovery scope.
enterprise.evalAssessmentDesc: Review organizational requirements: SSO, scale, data retention, governance model, integration fit, and stakeholder visibility needs.
enterprise.evalPilotDesc: Run a scoped pilot with enterprise stakeholders — validate workflows, security posture, and adoption on active projects.
enterprise.evalValidationDesc: Score pilot outcomes against your readiness checklist — access control, audit trails, AI review, and operational fit.
enterprise.evalRolloutDesc: Expand to additional projects or divisions with agreed governance — roles, templates, and review paths standardized.
enterprise.evalExpansionDesc: Multi-site or enterprise-wide deployment when criteria are met — commercial scope and engagement models are agreed via Pricing and Contact.

implementation.title: Implementation
implementation.metaDescription: How teams adopt AISTROYKA — deployment phases, role readiness, pilot scope, and rollout risks. Honest Live, Partial, and Planned labels; commercial terms on Pricing.
implementation.heroSubtitle: Deployment phases, role onboarding, and pilot scope — what exists in product today vs what we scope together on Contact. Not pricing, security depth, or feature catalog.
implementation.phasesSubtitle: A typical adoption path — phase depth varies by team size and scope. Commercial packaging lives on Pricing; intake lives on Contact.
implementation.phaseDiscoveryDesc: Align on active projects, roles, reporting habits, and pilot success criteria — primarily via Contact and pilot planning, not a self-serve wizard.
implementation.phasePilotDesc: Scoped usage on live work — launch from the dashboard or start via Contact. Validate field capture, manager review, and operational fit before expansion.
implementation.phaseConfigurationDesc: Workspace setup in product: tenant creation, projects, team invites, stakeholder invites, and role assignment — live self-serve and invite flows.
implementation.phaseTrainingDesc: In-app Get Started checklist, help hints, and short field walkthroughs — not a multi-week training program or LMS.
implementation.phaseRolloutDesc: Expand to additional projects or sites after pilot validation — scoped commercially via Contact and Pricing, not instant multi-site automation.
implementation.phaseExpansionDesc: Organizational expansion with governance alignment — enterprise evaluation on Enterprise; implementation detail stays on this page.
implementation.adoptionSubtitle: What each role can onboard to today — link to Mobile for field depth, not feature marketing here.
implementation.adoptWorkersDesc: iOS Worker app with structured daily-report flows; join via team invite. Short on-site walkthrough — confirm Android scope before standardizing non-iOS fleets.
implementation.adoptManagersDesc: Web and iOS Manager surfaces, team invites, project bootstrap, Get Started checklist, and report review inbox — primary pilot adoption path today.
implementation.adoptOwnersDesc: Configured stakeholder visibility after invite — customer-facing progress and commercial artifacts you choose to expose, not internal contractor finance.
implementation.adoptStakeholdersDesc: Stakeholder invite tokens, portal onboarding, and scoped project/client views — live invite and accept flows with path guards.
implementation.pilotSubtitle: Concrete in-product and operational checkpoints — not a guaranteed dedicated implementation team unless scoped on Contact.
implementation.pilotScopeDesc: Usually one project (or a tight portfolio slice) with defined reporting and review goals — timing is scope-dependent, not a fixed go-live promise.
implementation.pilotWorkspaceDesc: Onboarding wizard creates tenant and owner membership; invites add managers, members, and field roles; activation status tracks Get Started progress.
implementation.pilotFieldCaptureDesc: Workers and managers submit daily reports and evidence; data syncs when connectivity allows — confirm offline expectations for your scope.
implementation.pilotManagerReviewDesc: Managers review submissions, approve or request changes, and iterate templates from real site feedback.
implementation.pilotFeedbackDesc: Pilot learnings inform rollout scope — commercial next steps via Contact and Pricing, not automatic expansion.
implementation.risksSubtitle: Patterns we see when adoption stalls — mitigate during pilot, not after expansion.
implementation.riskScopeCreepDesc: Adding modules, sites, or roles before the pilot proves reporting discipline and manager review — keep the first scope narrow.
implementation.riskConnectivityDesc: Unstable site networks delay sync; do not assume full offline parity for every workflow until confirmed for your pilot.
implementation.riskRolesDesc: Mixing internal managers with portal stakeholders without clear invites leads to wrong surfaces — use stakeholder invites for external viewers.
implementation.riskDevicesDesc: Standardizing on Android before confirming parity can block field rollout — iOS Manager and Worker are the primary pilot contour today.
implementation.riskReviewDisciplineDesc: Treating AI summaries or field submissions as final without inbox review undermines accountability — keep human approval in the loop.

implementation.relatedContactDesc: Discovery intake, pilot discussion, and presentation requests.
